subject: Sentinel-7x sequence-level p95 drift — request for rollback gate review

From: Atlas Retail Ops <ops@atlasretail.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden tail-latency increase (sentinel-7x)

Hi Soojin —

We're seeing a sustained uptick in sequence-level p95 for model sentinel-7x after the 2028-05-13 rollout (v7x.2 -> v7x.3). The impacted endpoints are /generate and /chat-stream; p95 has moved from ~340ms to ~820ms for traffic coming from our US-West cluster. This started ~02:30 UTC on 2028-05-14 and has persisted despite restarting pods.

We've pulled a short HAR and a canary metrics export; attached. Notably:
- CPU utilization on the instance pool is steady, but token processing latency per-step spikes at sequence lengths > 512.
- KV cache hit rates are lower than usual for the same session tokens.

This is a production customer of ours (promotion scheduled next month); can you advise whether there's a rollback gate we can request and the fastest path to revert to v7x.2? We need an ETA on mitigation.

Thanks,
David
David Lopez
Head of Platform Reliability, Atlas Retail
ops@atlasretail.com

Hi David — thanks for the data. I'm looking at the attachments now. A few quick asks while we triage:

1) Can you confirm the request id(s) for two sample requests that hit the p95? (we only need the request_id so we can trace the tokenization path)
2) Was there any model-compiler change in the rollout notes other than the weight swap?

Operationally: we have an emergency rollback path for Dedicated and Hosted customers. Given this is an Atlas customer on Dedicated capacity, we can propose a temporary rollback to v7x.2 if internal approval is granted by the incident reviewer. Ben — can you weigh in on rollback gating? Marissa — can you confirm SLA carveout language if we go to a rollback and need short-term latency tolerance while we validate?

I'll hold on making any change until we have internal signoff, but we can prepare the rollback runbook (I attached the template).

Best,
Soojin Lee
